title: A reported SNAP theft can produce a replacement credit while leaving adequacy and household recovery unresolved
source_unit: Connecticut DSS/OLCRAH Notice of Decision, Request No. 226201
geography: Connecticut SNAP household; Connecticut Department of Social Services administrative hearing

observations.period: 2023 administrative decision; transaction, report, replacement, and hearing dates redacted in the public PDF

denominator.unit: anonymized OLCRAH administrative case; not a replacement-rate or household-outcome denominator

covered_loss.unit: U.S. dollars in SNAP loss found covered by the decision; the appellant claimed a larger amount

replacement_credit.unit: U.S. dollars reported by the agency as issued to the SNAP EBT account with a new card

appeal_and_residual_claim.value: The appellant reported the theft, requested a new card, submitted Form W-3037, filed a police report through her daughter, and appealed for an additional $2,125.34; OLCRAH upheld the agency limit and denied the residual appeal

receipt_and_adequacy.unit: missing transaction-level receipt confirmation, food purchases, interim food access, bills, debt, adequacy, later SNAP continuity, recurrence, trust, action, and exit

mechanism.value: An agency-recorded replacement can restore some nominal purchasing capacity while the replacement cap, redacted timing, and residual denial leave the household's usable food access and recovery unresolved

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Connecticut OLCRAH decision; theft report, card replacement, agency-recorded credit, appeal, and downstream non-observation are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision anonymizes the appellant and redacts dates. It does not provide independent account confirmation, transaction-level receipt or use, interim food access, amount adequacy, later benefit continuity, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: One anonymized Connecticut SNAP administrative case; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: The household may have remained food secure through other resources, or remained insecure despite the credit; an administrative replacement record does not establish either outcome.

observations.period: 2024 administrative decision; stolen SNAP transactions, initial denial, and corrective remand

denominator.unit: anonymized OLCRAH administrative case; not a replacement-rate or household-outcome denominator

covered_loss.unit: U.S. dollars in unauthorized SNAP transactions identified in the decision

initial_administrative_route.value: DSS issued a replacement EBT card but denied replacement of the stolen benefits because the completed request form was received 32 days after discovery

institutional_correction.value: The hearing officer granted the appeal, found that DSS had not shown timely notice of the required form, rescinded the denial, and ordered DSS to process the request as timely

replacement_receipt_and_adequacy.unit: missing later replacement credit, food purchases, interim food access, adequacy, household recovery, recurrence, trust, action, and exit

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Connecticut OLCRAH decision; unauthorized transactions, replacement-card issuance, denial, hearing correction, and downstream non-observation are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision anonymizes the appellant and redacts dates. It records a corrective order but not whether the later replacement was issued, received, or adequate, nor whether food access or household security recovered.
observations.subgroup: One anonymized Connecticut SNAP administrative case involving a stolen-benefit replacement request; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Correcting an administrative denial can restore a procedural route without proving that the household ultimately received benefits, avoided a food gap, or regained durable security.

boundary: This record establishes two anonymized Connecticut administrative cases: one agency-recorded partial replacement with residual denial, and one corrective hearing order reversing a stolen-benefit denial. It does not establish independent recipient receipt, later replacement issuance, benefit adequacy, food security, household recovery, population rates, durable trust, action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the published administrative decision; identifying fields, raw EBT transactions, and household follow-up records are not retained.
